tests.exercises: Simulator orchestration, spin-system setup, method execution and spectrum assembly
tests.why: Core public API regression; deterministic spectrum observables admit pointwise comparison and reject changes to orchestration or native-kernel results.

tests.exercises: Root-level constructors and serialization helpers
tests.why: API and data-model contracts are discrete structural invariants rather than long numerical trajectories.

tests.exercises: Transition amplitudes and pathway weighting
tests.why: Amplitude values are deterministic and physically observable; pointwise bounds catch normalization and transition-weight regressions.

tests.exercises: Angular-momentum and Wigner-element primitives
tests.why: Selection rules, Hermitian relations and tensor dimensions are exact mathematical invariants.

tests.exercises: Python bindings to native C interpolation, histogram and vector kernels
tests.why: Native kernel outputs are deterministic arrays; pointwise comparison detects ABI, indexing and floating-point regressions.

tests.exercises: Rotor-phase and gamma-angle sampling
tests.why: Periodicity, ordering and normalization of angular grids are invariant physical constraints.

tests.exercises: Orientation grids and triangular interpolation used by powder averaging
tests.why: Interpolated frequencies and weights have deterministic reference arrays; pointwise policy targets sampling and interpolation accuracy.

tests.exercises: Complex phase accumulation and phase cycling
tests.why: Phase factors have deterministic complex outputs; pointwise comparison catches sign and convention errors.

tests.exercises: Frequency-axis shifts and tensor-frequency contributions
tests.why: Chemical-shift observables are deterministic; pointwise tolerance detects frequency-contribution regressions.

tests.exercises: Vector and matrix math helpers used by native kernels
tests.why: Norms, products and shape contracts are algebraic invariants and remain stable across platforms.

tests.exercises: End-to-end 1D lineshape simulation and powder averaging
tests.why: The simulated spectrum is the primary physical observable; pointwise spectral comparison is the strongest regression signal.

tests.exercises: Coupled-site transition enumeration and spectrum synthesis
tests.why: Coupling changes transition frequencies and intensities deterministically; pointwise checks preserve the coupled-spectrum observable.

tests.exercises: Custom orientation sampling and weighted spectrum integration
tests.why: Custom sampling is deterministic and directly affects spectral amplitudes; pointwise comparison detects weighting or grid regressions.

tests.exercises: 1D two-quantum buildup method
tests.why: Official method regression with deterministic spectrum output; pointwise policy preserves the two-quantum observable.

tests.exercises: 2D MQMAS method and correlated spectral dimensions
tests.why: 2D spectral arrays are deterministic physical observables; pointwise checks cover both dimensions and interpolation.

tests.exercises: 2D STMAS satellite-transition simulation
tests.why: Satellite-transition spectra are deterministic; pointwise comparison catches method-path and quadrupolar-frequency errors.

tests.exercises: 2D dynamic-angle-spinning simulation
tests.why: DAS output is a deterministic 2D spectrum; pointwise bounds preserve angle-dependent frequencies and intensities.

tests.exercises: Sideband-sideband correlation spectrum
tests.why: Sideband correlation is deterministic and directly tests anisotropic frequency contributions.

tests.exercises: Wigner rotation matrices used in tensor orientation transforms
tests.why: Rotation matrices have deterministic reference values; pointwise checks catch orientation-transform regressions.

tests.exercises: Transition connectivity under angular-momentum rotations
tests.why: Connectivity and selection rules are discrete invariants, not trajectory-like floating-point observables.
